subject: Turning drawings into manufactured components
hook: What happens between you sending a drawing and collecting the parts.
ig:
What happens between you sending a drawing and collecting the parts.

A typical trade order through our workshop runs in six stages:

1. Your drawing or cutting list comes in.
2. We cross-check it and raise any questions before a single board is cut.
3. Cutting to finished size, following grain on woodgrain decors.
4. ABS edging on the edges you specified.
5. Drilling and labelling, so every part matches your list.
6. Collection, delivery or workshop assembly.

Stage two is the one that saves the most time. A five-minute question about a grain direction or a missing edge code is far cheaper than recutting a door.

If you are a fitter or maker with a run of jobs in the new year, this is how we would handle them. Send a list through the link in bio and ask for a price.
fb:
Here is what a typical trade order looks like once it lands with us.

We check your drawing or list first and ask any questions before cutting. Then it is cut, edged, drilled and labelled in our Hanley workshop, ready for you to collect, have delivered, or have us assemble.

The checking stage is the one people do not see, and it is the one that stops expensive recuts.

If you have a job on the board for January, send it over and we will price it:

alt: Six-frame carousel following a trade order: a drawing, a checked cutting list, a panel saw, an edge bander, a boring machine and labelled panels on a trolley.
on_asset: F1: Drawing in | You send drawings or a cutting list. We check sizes, board, grain, edging and drilling notes against each other. | F2: Questions answered | Anything unclear is raised before cutting, not after. You confirm the final list and receive an itemised price. | F3: Cut | Boards are cut to finished sizes on our sliding table panel saw, with grain direction followed on woodgrain decors. | F4: Edged | ABS edging applied on the edge bander to every edge you specified, at 0.4, 1 or 2 mm. | F5: Drilled and labelled | Hinge cups, shelf-pin rows and dowels on the multi-spindle boring machine. Every part referenced to your list. | F6: Ready to build | Collect from the workshop, have it delivered, or let us assemble the cabinets.
